editorial:
You follow nine-year-old Carlitos, who lives with his grandmother in Mexico while his mother Rosario works illegally in Los Angeles to send money home. When his grandmother passes away, Carlitos decides to cross the border alone to find her. Along the way he meets Enrique, a young man who starts out annoyed but slowly becomes a protector. The story moves between both sides of the border, showing two people who miss each other every single day. It is warm, emotional, and full of heart, with a strong focus on family and hope.

The acting is the real standout, especially the young lead who carries the whole movie with honesty and charm. The pacing keeps you invested without feeling rushed, and the emotional beats land naturally. Some moments feel a little predictable, and a few side characters are thin, but the core story stays strong. If you enjoy heartfelt family dramas, this is a great pick.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Carlitos finally reaches Los Angeles after a dangerous journey across the border. He finds the park where his mother waits every Sunday for his phone call. Rosario, who had been close to giving up and returning to Mexico, is stunned to see him. They run to each other and embrace, ending their separation. The film closes on their reunion, showing that love and determination can bridge even the hardest distance.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt family dramas and stories about love across borders.
